rewrite_for_speech_prompt_template.value:
This is one page from a book, but it reads as headings/a table of contents, not prose - reading it aloud word-for-word would sound like a jumbled list. Rewrite it as 1-3 short, natural spoken sentences describing what this page actually contains (e.g. "This page lists the table of contents" or "This page starts Chapter Three: Moving Deeply into the Now"). Only describe what is genuinely here - never invent content, opinions, or details not present in the text below.

"""{cleaned}"""
rewrite_for_speech_prompt_template.description: Rewrites a non-prose page (headings/TOC) into natural spoken sentences before TTS. Needs a {cleaned} placeholder.

generate_questions_prompt_template.value:
Here is a page from a book someone was just read out loud:

"""{page_text}"""

Write exactly {count} short comprehension questions about what this specific page actually said - nothing about the rest of the book, nothing invented. Someone who listened to this page should be able to answer each one directly from it.
generate_questions_prompt_template.description: Generates next-day comprehension quiz questions for a read page. Needs {page_text} and {count} placeholders.

prompt_with_emotions_prompt_template.value:
You are a text-formatting tool that inserts emotion tags into book text for a TTS voice. You do not explain, summarize, or comment - you only return the tagged text.

Here is one page from a book, about to be read aloud by a text-to-speech voice that understands a small set of emotion tags embedded directly in the text.

Add emotion tags ONLY where the text clearly calls for them. Use only these tags, exactly as written: <laugh> <chuckle> <sigh> <gasp> <yawn> <cough> <sniffle> <groan>

Rules:
- If a real, present character in a conversation actually makes one of these sounds - gasps, sighs, laughs, coughs, sniffles - tag it. This is the normal, common case in a book with dialogue; most pages with real conversation in them will have at least one.
- Only skip a tag when the word is NOT describing a real person's sound - narration about weather/objects/machines ("the wind sighed," "the engine gave a sigh"), or an idiom ("he coughed up the cash" means he paid reluctantly, nobody coughed). These are the exception, not the default - most uses of these words in a real conversation ARE real sounds and DO get tagged.
- The tag is ADDED NEXT TO the original word - it never replaces it. Example: the original text "she gasped, stepping back" becomes "she gasped <gasp>, stepping back" - CORRECT (the word "gasped" is still there, the tag sits right after it). It must NEVER become "she <gasp>, stepping back" - WRONG (the word "gasped" is gone, only the tag remains). This applies to every tag you add, every time, with no exceptions.
- Return the page's text completely unchanged, word for word, everywhere else - the only thing you may add is the tags themselves. Never rewrite, shorten, summarize, paraphrase, or invent any part of it.
- Match the tag to the emotion precisely - a light laugh is <chuckle>, not <laugh>; shock is <gasp>, not <sigh>; tiredness is <yawn>, not <sigh>. The tag for a sniffling/crying sound is spelled <sniffle> - NOT <sniff>, even though the word in the text is often "sniff" or "sniffed." Use only the 8 exact tag names given above, character for character - never a variant, abbreviation, or the trigger word itself wrapped in brackets.

"""{page_text}"""

Reminder before you answer: (1) look through the conversation above for every real character sound - gasped, sighed, laughed, coughed, sniffled, groaned, chuckled, yawned - and tag each genuine one; don't skip a real sound out of excess caution. The only ones to skip are non-human uses (weather, machines, scenery) and idioms ("coughed up the cash") where nobody actually made that sound. (2) Every tag you add must sit NEXT TO the original word, which stays in the text exactly as it was - "gasped <gasp>" is correct, "<gasp>" alone in place of "gasped" is wrong, every single time. Reply with ONLY the resulting text - no preamble, no explanation, no markdown, no quotes around it.
prompt_with_emotions_prompt_template.description: Inserts Orpheus emotion tags (<laugh> <chuckle> <sigh> <gasp> <yawn> <cough> <sniffle> <groan>) into a page's text before TTS, restricted to real character reactions during dialogue - never scenery/idiom. Needs a {page_text} placeholder.

business_persona_context.description: Free-text instructions for how AdiyanReader should sound and reason when generating quiz questions or speech-formatting text on behalf of a specific business's customer. Empty on the platform layer by default; a real value only comes from a vertical override written by mesh/config_agent/skills/apply_vertical_spec.py. Applied only when the sender is not the owner - see mesh/lib/persona_hook.py's own docstring.
